newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up, dollar, Germany setting agenda.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up, dollar, Germany setting agenda.

text.p: Danish bond prices were slightly up on Wednesday in a nervous market steered by the dollar and Germany.
"Mark-dollar developments are steering market trends, there is still some nervousness about a possible variable German repo rate being imposed, so players are wary," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.06 point from the opening at 112.54, yielding 6.07 percent. The seven percent 2007 state bond, due to become benchmark on September 1, also put on 0.06 point, climbing to 105.42, with the yield at 6.26 percent.
Turnover in the keynote 2006 and 2007 bonds was 1.3 billion and 670 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future fell 0.12 point to 112.18 with 46 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.25 point to 91.45.
The crown traded at 3.8115 per mark at 1105 GMT, down a tad from around 3.8110 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two basis points to 57 bps during the course of the morning.
